response.original_text: JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release. The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal. “The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision. “In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added. Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.” Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest. He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025. | via Janvic Mateo

citations.quote: Piroschka van de Wouw/Pool via Reuters MANILA, Philippines – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III ordered the continued detention of former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte at The Hague, Netherlands.

“The Chamber therefore finds no notable change in circumstances that warrant the release of the Accused, with or without conditions. For these reasons, the chamber hereby decides that the accused shall continue to be detained,” said the chamber’s decision on Wednesday, September 16.
According to the trial chamber, it found that there’s a likelihood that Duterte would “abscond,” “obstruct,” or “endanger” the court proceedings.

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the court explained.
But even though the results of this assessment are still pending, the “panel’s reports do not contain any information that warrants a modification of the accused’s detention,” the court said.

“Accordingly, the Chamber finds that the risks under Article 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) have increased and, in respect of the risks outlined in Article 58(1)(b)(iii), sees no change in circumstances,” the court explained.

content_profile.verification_text:
JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release.
The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal.
“The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision.
“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added.
Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.”
Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest.
He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025.
